overview: The Council approved special permits and storage licenses for a new luxury auto dealership and received a milestone report from the Health Department regarding the conclusion of COVID-19 restrictions. Members also addressed a 15-month vacancy in the Sealer of Weights and Measures position and discussed filing public records requests to compel the administration to disclose legal expenditures.

items.title: Public Hearing: Herb Chambers BMW Special Permit
items.summary: Approved a special permit for Class II used auto sales and Class IV auto repair at 60 Mystic Avenue with a condition prohibiting outdoor intercom use and a scheduled six-month review.

items.title: Public Hearing: Flammable Storage License
items.summary: Approved a flammable storage license for oil and fluids at 60 Mystic Avenue, contingent on final approval from the Fire and Building Departments after installation.

items.title: Public Health Update: COVID-19 Milestone
items.summary: Public Health Director MaryAnn O'Connor reported that the city reached a milestone of zero new cases over three days and noted that Medford's vaccination rate stands at approximately 60%.

items.title: Recognition of Eagle Scout Derek Julio
items.summary: The Council honored Derek Julio with a citation for achieving the rank of Eagle Scout following his community service project to improve church property on Otis Street.

items.title: Sealer of Weights and Measures Inquiry
items.summary: Approved a resolution requesting a list of inspected entities and the identity of the Sealer of Weights and Measures amid concerns the post has been vacant since March 2020.

items.title: Condon Shell Dock Mitigation
items.summary: Approved a resolution asking the administration to negotiate the installation of a small dock at the Condon Shell as mitigation for commercial riverfront use.

items.title: Verizon Grant of Location: Boston Avenue
items.summary: Tabled a petition for underground conduits to support the Green Line Extension until Verizon removes an unrelated double utility pole at Greenleaf and Burget Avenues.

items.title: Loan Order: $1,222,000 Water Bonds
items.summary: Referred a request to borrow $1.2 million for water main improvements on six city streets to the Committee of the Whole for further financial vetting.

items.title: Discussion on Legal Expenditure Transparency
items.summary: Councilors discussed using the Public Records Act to obtain a breakdown of legal spending with KP Law after the administration failed to respond to multiple previous information requests.

items.title: Public Participation
items.summary: Residents addressed the need for local public access television for candidates, safety concerns regarding a new traffic island at High and Woburn Streets, and alternatives to armed police response.
